components.label: 240 V study supply · Ireland nominal 230 V

activities.title: Inspect 240 V study supply · Ireland nominal 230 V
activities.instruction: Open 240 V study supply · Ireland nominal 230 V and choose Show terminals. Find where its wires go.
activities.explanation: Virtual customer supply with explicitly modelled source impedance. The service equipment is a contextual boundary.

activities.title: Inspect Meter · energy boundary
activities.instruction: Open Meter · energy boundary and choose Show terminals. Find where its wires go.
activities.explanation: A supply meter records energy in kilowatt-hours. Its practice display shows the power passing through its own line connection right now, in kilowatts (kW).

activities.title: Inspect Customer main isolator
activities.instruction: Open Customer main isolator and choose Show terminals. Find where its wires go.
activities.explanation: Linked line and neutral contacts provide local isolation.

activities.title: Inspect Consumer unit overview
activities.instruction: Open Consumer unit overview and choose Show terminals. Find where its wires go.
activities.explanation: Openable cabinet with DIN rails, conductor bars, circuit labels and a customer-side supply path.

activities.title: Inspect Illustrative outgoing MCB
activities.instruction: Open Illustrative outgoing MCB and choose Show terminals. Find where its wires go.
activities.explanation: Overcurrent protection with a thermal and magnetic conceptual mechanism.

activities.title: Inspect Represented outgoing circuit
activities.instruction: Open Represented outgoing circuit and choose Show terminals. Find where its wires go.
activities.explanation: An illustrative resistive lamp load with animated illumination.

activities.title: What do you expect?
activities.instruction: You open the main switch. What happens to the light?
activities.explanation: The meter counts the energy used. The main switch disconnects the board. The supply side of the switch can still be live.

options.label: It goes out
It stays on while the meter has power

activities.title: Connect 240 V study supply · Ireland nominal 230 V · L to Meter · energy boundary · L
activities.instruction: With the simulated supply off, connect 240 V study supply · Ireland nominal 230 V · L to Meter · energy boundary · L. Use the core marked L.
activities.explanation: Line brings power to the fitting. Its usual marking is L. → Line brings power to the fitting. Its usual marking is L.

activities.title: Connect 240 V study supply · Ireland nominal 230 V · N to Meter · energy boundary · N
activities.instruction: With the simulated supply off, connect 240 V study supply · Ireland nominal 230 V · N to Meter · energy boundary · N. Use the core marked N.
activities.explanation: Neutral carries current back to the supply while the load is on. → Neutral carries current back to the supply while the load is on.

activities.title: Connect 240 V study supply · Ireland nominal 230 V · PE to Meter · energy boundary · PE
activities.instruction: With the simulated supply off, connect 240 V study supply · Ireland nominal 230 V · PE to Meter · energy boundary · PE. Use the core marked PE.
activities.explanation: Supply earth. The earth connection runs alongside the meter. → Supply earth. The earth connection runs alongside the meter.

activities.title: Connect Meter · energy boundary · LOUT to Customer main isolator · LIN
activities.instruction: With the simulated supply off, connect Meter · energy boundary · LOUT to Customer main isolator · LIN. Use the core marked L.
activities.explanation: Outgoing L terminal of its separately modelled linked contact path. Pair it with LIN. Matching phase/neutral identities matter; mechanical linkage does not join the poles electrically. → Incoming L terminal of its separately modelled linked contact path. Pair it with LOUT. Matching phase/neutral identities matter; mechanical linkage does not join the poles electrically.

activities.title: Connect Meter · energy boundary · NOUT to Customer main isolator · NIN
activities.instruction: With the simulated supply off, connect Meter · energy boundary · NOUT to Customer main isolator · NIN. Use the core marked N.
activities.explanation: Outgoing N terminal of its separately modelled linked contact path. Pair it with NIN. Matching phase/neutral identities matter; mechanical linkage does not join the poles electrically. → Incoming N terminal of its separately modelled linked contact path. Pair it with NOUT. Matching phase/neutral identities matter; mechanical linkage does not join the poles electrically.

activities.title: Connect Customer main isolator · LOUT to Consumer unit overview · L
activities.instruction: With the simulated supply off, connect Customer main isolator · LOUT to Consumer unit overview · L. Use the core marked L.
activities.explanation: Outgoing L terminal of its separately modelled linked contact path. Pair it with LIN. Matching phase/neutral identities matter; mechanical linkage does not join the poles electrically. → Line brings power to the fitting. Its usual marking is L.

activities.title: Connect Customer main isolator · NOUT to Consumer unit overview · N
activities.instruction: With the simulated supply off, connect Customer main isolator · NOUT to Consumer unit overview · N. Use the core marked N.
activities.explanation: Outgoing N terminal of its separately modelled linked contact path. Pair it with NIN. Matching phase/neutral identities matter; mechanical linkage does not join the poles electrically. → Neutral carries current back to the supply while the load is on.

activities.title: Connect Meter · energy boundary · PEOUT to Consumer unit overview · PE
activities.instruction: With the simulated supply off, connect Meter · energy boundary · PEOUT to Consumer unit overview · PE. Use the core marked PE.
activities.explanation: Supply earth. The earth connection runs alongside the meter. → Earth connection for the fitting. The earth path stays connected when the switch opens.

activities.title: Connect Consumer unit overview · LOUT to Illustrative outgoing MCB · IN
activities.instruction: With the simulated supply off, connect Consumer unit overview · LOUT to Illustrative outgoing MCB · IN. Use the core marked L.
activities.explanation: Outgoing L terminal of its separately modelled linked contact path. Pair it with LIN. Matching phase/neutral identities matter; mechanical linkage does not join the poles electrically. → First end of the modelled series protected path, paired with OUT. Opening or tripping the device separates this pair.

activities.title: Connect Illustrative outgoing MCB · OUT to Represented outgoing circuit · L
activities.instruction: With the simulated supply off, connect Illustrative outgoing MCB · OUT to Represented outgoing circuit · L. Use the core marked L.
activities.explanation: Second end of the modelled series protected path, paired with IN. Opening or tripping the device separates this pair. → Line brings power to the fitting. Its usual marking is L.

activities.title: Connect Consumer unit overview · NOUT to Represented outgoing circuit · N
activities.instruction: With the simulated supply off, connect Consumer unit overview · NOUT to Represented outgoing circuit · N. Use the core marked N.
activities.explanation: Outgoing N terminal of its separately modelled linked contact path. Pair it with NIN. Matching phase/neutral identities matter; mechanical linkage does not join the poles electrically. → Neutral carries current back to the supply while the load is on.

activities.title: Connect Consumer unit overview · PEOUT to Represented outgoing circuit · PE
activities.instruction: With the simulated supply off, connect Consumer unit overview · PEOUT to Represented outgoing circuit · PE. Use the core marked PE.
activities.explanation: Outgoing earth connection for the fitting. The earth path stays connected when the switch opens. → Earth connection for the fitting. The earth path stays connected when the switch opens.

activities.title: Enable the simulated supply
activities.instruction: After completing the connections, leave resistance mode, then turn on the supply.
activities.explanation: Use voltage mode to check a powered circuit. Switch off all sources before testing continuity.

activities.title: Normal operating request
activities.instruction: Watch what the circuit does now.
activities.explanation: light receives operating load power.

activities.title: Open main
activities.instruction: Open Customer main isolator.
activities.explanation: light operating load power stops.

activities.title: Restore main
activities.instruction: Close Customer main isolator.
activities.explanation: light receives operating load power.

activities.title: Measure across the load
activities.instruction: Place red on Represented outgoing circuit · L and black on Represented outgoing circuit · N. Record the voltage with the controls in this position.
activities.explanation: Compare line to neutral before and after the main switch. With that switch open, its supply side can still read close to mains voltage. If you see zero, check the switch position.

activities.title: Read the current in one wire
activities.instruction: Select the conductor from 240 V study supply · Ireland nominal 230 V · L to Meter · energy boundary · L and record the current in amps.
activities.explanation: The meter shows the current in this wire. Where the circuit splits, the branches can carry different currents.

activities.title: Check the wire for a break
activities.instruction: Turn off all sources, then measure resistance between Illustrative outgoing MCB · OUT and Represented outgoing circuit · L. Take the meter out of resistance mode before switching the power back on.
activities.explanation: A low resistance shows a path between the probes. If two wires reach the same point, the meter can still find a path around a break.

activities.title: What explains what you saw?
activities.instruction: Which device turned off the supply to the board?
activities.explanation: The meter counts the energy used. The main switch disconnects the board. The supply side of the switch can still be live.

options.label: The meter
The main switch

activities.title: Repair the fault
activities.instruction: Use your readings to find what went wrong. Repair it, then reset any device that tripped.
activities.explanation: Run a fresh test to check the repair.

activities.title: Retest the operating sequence
activities.instruction: Choose Test circuit to check your repair.
activities.explanation: The bench tries the lesson controls again using your wiring.

challenge.title: Diagnose: Single-phase supply, meter and consumer unit
challenge.briefing: The meter has a supply but the lamp is dark.
challenge.hint: Start at the outgoing breaker. Compare its output with the line terminal at the lamp.
challenge.answer: The wire from the breaker output to lamp L is open. Voltage at the meter tells you the incoming supply is present, but it doesn’t tell you that the lamp has a complete circuit.

challenge.title: Diagnose: Shared RCCB with outgoing MCB circuits
challenge.briefing: A fault on one circuit has tripped the shared device. Both loads are off.
challenge.hint: Look for the protective device common to the lamp and socket. Check its trip indication.
challenge.answer: Current is leaking to earth at the lamp load. The shared RCCB detects the imbalance and opens, cutting power to both branches.

activities.title: Connect 240 V study supply · Ireland nominal 230 V · L to Illustrative RCBO · 16 A / 30 mA · LIN

activities.title: Connect 240 V study supply · Ireland nominal 230 V · N to Illustrative RCBO · 16 A / 30 mA · NIN

activities.title: Enable the simulated supply
activities.instruction: After completing the connections, leave resistance mode, then turn on the supply.
activities.explanation: Use voltage mode to check a powered circuit. Switch off all sources before testing continuity.

activities.title: Parallel luminaires share their supply
activities.instruction: Watch what the circuit does now.
activities.explanation: light-a receives operating load power. light-b receives operating load power. light-c receives operating load power. Parallel luminaires receive nearly equal voltages.

expectedObservations.title: Parallel luminaires receive nearly equal voltages

activities.title: Measure across the load
activities.instruction: Place red on Parallel luminaire A · L and black on Parallel luminaire A · N. Record the voltage with the controls in this position.
activities.explanation: Read L to N at each lit lamp. Each should be close to the full supply. The shared feed carries the current for all the lamps that are on. If you see zero, check the switch position.

activities.title: Read the current in one wire
activities.instruction: Select the conductor from 240 V study supply · Ireland nominal 230 V · L to Illustrative RCBO · 16 A / 30 mA · LIN and record the current in amps.
activities.explanation: The meter shows the current in this wire. Where the circuit splits, the branches can carry different currents.

activities.title: Check the wire for a break
activities.instruction: Turn off all sources, then measure resistance between Illustrative RCBO · 16 A / 30 mA · NOUT and Parallel luminaire B · N. Take the meter out of resistance mode before switching the power back on.
activities.explanation: A low resistance shows a path between the probes. If two wires reach the same point, the meter can still find a path around a break.

activities.title: What explains what you saw?
activities.instruction: Where does each lamp get its voltage?
activities.explanation: Each lamp has its own path from the switched line to neutral. Electricians call that a parallel circuit.

options.label: Between the same switched line and neutral
Across one part of a chain of three lamps

activities.title: Repair the fault
activities.instruction: Use your readings to find what went wrong. Repair it, then reset any device that tripped.
activities.explanation: Run a fresh test to check the repair.

activities.title: Retest the operating sequence
activities.instruction: Choose Test circuit to check your repair.
activities.explanation: The bench tries the lesson controls again using your wiring.

challenge.title: Diagnose: Parallel lighting bank
challenge.briefing: One lamp is dark. The two beside it still work.
challenge.hint: Compare the dark lamp’s line and neutral connections with the working lamps.
challenge.answer: Lamp B has an open neutral wire. The other two branches still have complete return paths, so their lamps can stay on.

activities.title: Independent thermal limit opens with demand present
activities.instruction: Close Operating thermostat. Open Independent thermal cut-out.
activities.explanation: element operating load power stops.

activities.title: Measure across the load
activities.instruction: Place red on Immersion element · L and black on Immersion element · N. Record the voltage with the controls in this position.
activities.explanation: Compare the voltage across the element and across each contact. When an open contact interrupts heating, it can have voltage across it. If you see zero, check the switch position.

activities.title: Read the current in one wire
activities.instruction: Select the conductor from 240 V study supply · Ireland nominal 230 V · L to Illustrative RCBO · 16 A / 30 mA · LIN and record the current in amps.
activities.explanation: The meter shows the current in this wire. Where the circuit splits, the branches can carry different currents.

activities.title: Check the wire for a break
activities.instruction: Turn off all sources, then measure resistance between Operating thermostat · OUT and Independent thermal cut-out · COM. Take the meter out of resistance mode before switching the power back on.
activities.explanation: A low resistance shows a path between the probes. If two wires reach the same point, the meter can still find a path around a break.

activities.title: What explains what you saw?
activities.instruction: Why can either device stop the element?
activities.explanation: The thermostat regulates the water temperature. The cut-out can stop heating even if the thermostat stays closed.

options.label: Either contact can supply the element on its own
Current to the element passes through both contacts

activities.title: Repair the fault
activities.instruction: Use your readings to find what went wrong. Repair it, then reset any device that tripped.
activities.explanation: Run a fresh test to check the repair.

activities.title: Retest the operating sequence
activities.instruction: Choose Test circuit to check your repair.
activities.explanation: The bench tries the lesson controls again using your wiring.

challenge.title: Diagnose: Immersion thermostat and independent cut-out
challenge.briefing: The thermostat is calling for heat, but the element stays cold.
challenge.hint: Work from the thermostat output towards the input of the thermal cut-out.
challenge.answer: The wire from thermostat OUT to cut-out COM is open. Even with both controls closed, heating current cannot cross the break.

challenge.title: Diagnose: Boiler programmer and room demand
challenge.briefing: The programme is on and the room calls for heat, but the boiler does not respond.
challenge.hint: Compare the thermostat output with the terminal it feeds at the boiler.
challenge.answer: The wire from the thermostat output to the boiler input is open. A heat call at the thermostat cannot reach the boiler.

challenge.title: Diagnose: S-plan two-port zone controls
challenge.briefing: With only the heating zone calling, its valve opens but the boiler stays off.

challenge.answer: The wire from the heating valve end switch to the boiler-call junction is open. The cylinder end switch can still call the boiler and mask the break.

activities.title: Enable the simulated supply
activities.instruction: After completing the connections, leave resistance mode, then turn on the supply.
activities.explanation: Use voltage mode to check a powered circuit. Switch off all sources before testing continuity.

activities.title: Floor condition permits heating
activities.instruction: Watch what the circuit does now.
activities.explanation: mat receives operating load power.

activities.title: Floor condition exceeds setpoint
activities.instruction: Set the reading on Floor-temperature probe interface to 40 °C.
activities.explanation: mat operating load power stops.

activities.title: Measure across the load
activities.instruction: Place red on Electric underfloor mat · L and black on Electric underfloor mat · N. Record the voltage with the controls in this position.
activities.explanation: Read across the mat with the floor below and above its limit. The controller can still have mains power when mat voltage is near zero. If you see zero, check the switch position.

activities.title: Read the current in one wire
activities.instruction: Select the conductor from 240 V study supply · Ireland nominal 230 V · L to Illustrative RCBO · 16 A / 30 mA · LIN and record the current in amps.
activities.explanation: The meter shows the current in this wire. Where the circuit splits, the branches can carry different currents.

activities.title: Check the wire for a break
activities.instruction: Turn off all sources, then measure resistance between Floor-temperature probe interface · OUT and Underfloor room thermostat · COM. Take the meter out of resistance mode before switching the power back on.
activities.explanation: A low resistance shows a path between the probes. If two wires reach the same point, the meter can still find a path around a break.

activities.title: What explains what you saw?
activities.instruction: Which temperature does this probe measure?
activities.explanation: The floor probe limits the heat. Power can be available at the controller while the mat itself is off.

options.label: The air temperature at the wall switch
The floor temperature

activities.title: Repair the fault
activities.instruction: Use your readings to find what went wrong. Repair it, then reset any device that tripped.
activities.explanation: Run a fresh test to check the repair.

activities.title: Retest the operating sequence
activities.instruction: Choose Test circuit to check your repair.
activities.explanation: The bench tries the lesson controls again using your wiring.

challenge.title: Diagnose: Electric underfloor heating and floor limit
challenge.briefing: The room calls and the floor is below the limit, but the mat won’t heat.
challenge.hint: Compare the floor control output with the room thermostat input.
challenge.answer: The wire from the floor control output to the room thermostat is open. The room control can’t pass heat demand on to the mat.

activities.explanation: Line brings power to the fitting. Its usual marking is L. → Incoming L terminal of its separately modelled linked contact path. Pair it with LOUT. Matching phase/neutral identities matter; mechanical linkage does not join the poles electrically.

activities.title: Connect 240 V study supply · Ireland nominal 230 V · N to Illustrative RCBO · 16 A / 30 mA · NIN

activities.title: Connect Illustrative RCBO · 16 A / 30 mA · LOUT to Single-phase motor contactor · 1

activities.explanation: Outgoing L terminal of its separately modelled linked contact path. Pair it with LIN. Matching phase/neutral identities matter; mechanical linkage does not join the poles electrically. → Incoming side of power-contact pair 1–2. This pair closes when the contactor operates and opens when it releases. It is separate from the coil and auxiliary contacts.

activities.title: Connect Single-phase motor contactor · 2 to Motor overload · 1

activities.explanation: Outgoing side of power-contact pair 1–2. This pair closes when the contactor operates and opens when it releases. It is separate from the coil and auxiliary contacts. → Incoming side of motor-current sensing path 1–2. The overload checks the current through this pair. A trip opens the control contacts 95–96, allowing the contactor to cut the motor supply.

activities.title: Connect Motor overload · 2 to Single-phase motor · L
activities.instruction: With the simulated supply off, connect Motor overload · 2 to Single-phase motor · L. Use the core marked L.

activities.title: Connect Illustrative RCBO · 16 A / 30 mA · NOUT to Single-phase motor · N

activities.title: Connect Illustrative RCBO · 16 A / 30 mA · LOUT to Stop · normally closed · COM
activities.instruction: With the simulated supply off, connect Illustrative RCBO · 16 A / 30 mA · LOUT to Stop · normally closed · COM. Use the core marked control.
activities.explanation: Outgoing L terminal of its separately modelled linked contact path. Pair it with LIN. Matching phase/neutral identities matter; mechanical linkage does not join the poles electrically. → Common connection of the separate changeover contact. This is a supplied contact circuit, not the coil or a neutral reference.

activities.title: Connect Stop · normally closed · NC to Motor overload · 95
activities.instruction: With the simulated supply off, connect Stop · normally closed · NC to Motor overload · 95. Use the core marked control.
activities.explanation: Normally closed path from COM: opens when the button is held pressed and closes on release. It can interrupt a maintained request if wired in that request path. → Normally closed contacts 95–96. An overload trip opens them. When they are wired in series with the coil, the contactor drops out and the motor stops.

activities.title: Connect Motor overload · 96 to Start · momentary normally open · COM
activities.instruction: With the simulated supply off, connect Motor overload · 96 to Start · momentary normally open · COM. Use the core marked control.
activities.explanation: Normally closed contacts 95–96. An overload trip opens them. When they are wired in series with the coil, the contactor drops out and the motor stops. → Common connection of the separate changeover contact. This is a supplied contact circuit, not the coil or a neutral reference.

activities.title: Connect Motor overload · 96 to Single-phase motor contactor · 13
activities.instruction: With the simulated supply off, connect Motor overload · 96 to Single-phase motor contactor · 13. Use the core marked control.
activities.explanation: Normally closed contacts 95–96. An overload trip opens them. When they are wired in series with the coil, the contactor drops out and the motor stops. → Normally open auxiliary contacts. When the contactor pulls in, 13 joins 14. Wired across Start, this pair can keep the coil on after you let go.

activities.title: Connect Start · momentary normally open · NO to Single-phase motor contactor · A1

activities.explanation: Normally open path from COM: closes when the button is held pressed and opens on release. → Coil first connection, paired with A2. Measure across A1–A2 to see what voltage reaches the coil. The load current flows through separate contacts.

activities.title: Connect Single-phase motor contactor · 14 to Single-phase motor contactor · A1
activities.instruction: With the simulated supply off, connect Single-phase motor contactor · 14 to Single-phase motor contactor · A1. Use the core marked control.
activities.explanation: Normally open auxiliary contacts. When the contactor pulls in, 13 joins 14. Wired across Start, this pair can keep the coil on after you let go. → Coil first connection, paired with A2. Measure across A1–A2 to see what voltage reaches the coil. The load current flows through separate contacts.

activities.title: Connect Illustrative RCBO · 16 A / 30 mA · NOUT to Single-phase motor contactor · A2
activities.instruction: With the simulated supply off, connect Illustrative RCBO · 16 A / 30 mA · NOUT to Single-phase motor contactor · A2. Use the core marked N.
activities.explanation: Outgoing N terminal of its separately modelled linked contact path. Pair it with NIN. activities.title: What explains what you saw?
activities.instruction: Which contact keeps the coil powered once Start opens again?
activities.explanation: Start briefly energises the coil. A small extra contact closes around Start and keeps the coil on. Stop breaks that path.

The motor’s main power contact alone

challenge.title: Diagnose: Single-phase start/stop motor starter
challenge.briefing: The motor runs while you hold Start and stops as soon as you let go.
challenge.hint: Trace auxiliary terminal 14 to A1 on the starter.
challenge.answer: The link from 14 to A1 is open. The Start button can supply the coil directly, but the holding contact has no route to keep it energised.

activities.explanation: Outgoing N terminal of its separately modelled linked contact path. Pair it with NIN. Matching phase/neutral identities matter; mechanical linkage does not join the poles electrically. → Neutral carries current back to the supply while the load is on.

activities.title: Connect Illustrative RCBO · 16 A / 30 mA · LOUT to Load-management permission · IN
activities.instruction: With the simulated supply off, connect Illustrative RCBO · 16 A / 30 mA · LOUT to Load-management permission · IN. Use the core marked control.
activities.explanation: Outgoing L terminal of its separately modelled linked contact path. Pair it with LIN. Matching phase/neutral identities matter; mechanical linkage does not join the poles electrically. → Wired permission input, sensed relative to N. A connected IN path must carry sufficient input voltage before the declared condition/timer can request the output. It is not a dry-contact output.

activities.title: Connect Load-management permission · OUT to EVSE charge-permission interface · A1
activities.instruction: With the simulated supply off, connect Load-management permission · OUT to EVSE charge-permission interface · A1. Use the core marked control.
activities.explanation: Powered switched output from L. Its contact closes only when the controller is supplied and the wired permission, environmental condition and declared delay permit operation. OUT is not isolated from this controller supply. → Coil first connection, paired with A2. Measure across A1–A2 to see what voltage reaches the coil. The load current flows through separate contacts.

activities.title: Connect Illustrative RCBO · 16 A / 30 mA · NOUT to EVSE charge-permission interface · A2
activities.instruction: With the simulated supply off, connect Illustrative RCBO · 16 A / 30 mA · NOUT to EVSE charge-permission interface · A2. Use the core marked N.
activities.explanation: Outgoing N terminal of its separately modelled linked contact path. Pair it with NIN. Matching phase/neutral identities matter; mechanical linkage does not join the poles electrically. → Coil return connection, paired with A1. Measure across A1–A2 to see what voltage reaches the coil. The load current flows through separate contacts.

activities.title: Connect Illustrative RCBO · 16 A / 30 mA · LOUT to EVSE charge-permission interface · 1
activities.instruction: With the simulated supply off, connect Illustrative RCBO · 16 A / 30 mA · LOUT to EVSE charge-permission interface · 1. Use the core marked L.
activities.explanation: Outgoing L terminal of its separately modelled linked contact path. Pair it with LIN. Matching phase/neutral identities matter; mechanical linkage does not join the poles electrically. → Incoming side of power-contact pair 1–2. This pair closes when the contactor operates and opens when it releases. It is separate from the coil and auxiliary contacts.

activities.title: Connect EVSE charge-permission interface · 2 to Single-phase EVSE · packaged controls · L
activities.instruction: With the simulated supply off, connect EVSE charge-permission interface · 2 to Single-phase EVSE · packaged controls · L. Use the core marked L.
activities.explanation: Outgoing side of power-contact pair 1–2. This pair closes when the contactor operates and opens when it releases. It is separate from the coil and auxiliary contacts. → Line brings power to the fitting. Its usual marking is L.

activities.title: Connect Illustrative RCBO · 16 A / 30 mA · NOUT to Single-phase EVSE · packaged controls · N
activities.instruction: With the simulated supply off, connect Illustrative RCBO · 16 A / 30 mA · NOUT to Single-phase EVSE · packaged controls · N. Use the core marked N.
activities.explanation: Outgoing N terminal of its separately modelled linked contact path. Pair it with NIN. Matching phase/neutral identities matter; mechanical linkage does not join the poles electrically. → Neutral carries current back to the supply while the load is on.

activities.title: Connect 240 V study supply · Ireland nominal 230 V · PE to Single-phase EVSE · packaged controls · PE
activities.instruction: With the simulated supply off, connect 240 V study supply · Ireland nominal 230 V · PE to Single-phase EVSE · packaged controls · PE. Use the core marked PE.
activities.explanation: Supply earth. The earth connection runs alongside the meter. → Earth connection for the fitting. The earth path stays connected when the switch opens.

activities.title: Enable the simulated supply
activities.instruction: After completing the connections, leave resistance mode, then turn on the supply.
activities.explanation: Use voltage mode to check a powered circuit. Switch off all sources before testing continuity.

activities.title: Charge permission present
activities.instruction: Watch what the circuit does now.
activities.explanation: evse receives operating load power.

activities.title: Remove charge permission
activities.instruction: Stop the call from Load-management permission.
activities.explanation: evse operating load power stops.

activities.title: Measure across the load
activities.instruction: Place red on Single-phase EVSE · packaged controls · L and black on Single-phase EVSE · packaged controls · N. Record the voltage with the controls in this position.
activities.explanation: Read from the incoming line to neutral, then from charger L to N. Here the incoming side stays at mains voltage when the contactor opens and the charger loses its feed. If you see zero, check the switch position.

activities.title: Read the current in one wire
activities.instruction: Select the conductor from 240 V study supply · Ireland nominal 230 V · L to Illustrative RCBO · 16 A / 30 mA · LIN and record the current in amps.
activities.explanation: The meter shows the current in this wire. Where the circuit splits, the branches can carry different currents.

activities.title: Check the wire for a break
activities.instruction: Turn off all sources, then measure resistance between Load-management permission · OUT and EVSE charge-permission interface · A1. Take the meter out of resistance mode before switching the power back on.
activities.explanation: A low resistance shows a path between the probes. If two wires reach the same point, the meter can still find a path around a break.

activities.title: What explains what you saw?
activities.instruction: The contactor has opened. Which side still has a mains supply?
activities.explanation: Here an electrically operated switch, the contactor, cuts the feed to the charger. The site supply and the load controller stay on.

options.label: The incoming side from the board
The outgoing side feeding this charger

activities.title: Repair the fault
activities.instruction: Use your readings to find what went wrong. Repair it, then reset any device that tripped.
activities.explanation: Run a fresh test to check the repair.

activities.title: Retest the operating sequence
activities.instruction: Choose Test circuit to check your repair.
activities.explanation: The bench tries the lesson controls again using your wiring.

challenge.title: Diagnose: EVSE supply and load-management permission
challenge.briefing: The site has power and the controller calls for charging, but the car load stays off.
challenge.hint: Compare controller OUT with the voltage across A1–A2 at the charge contactor.
challenge.answer: The wire from controller OUT to A1 is open. The contactor cannot pull in, so its main contact leaves the charger without a live feed.

activities.explanation: Separate phase, neutral and protective contacts for industrial equipment.

activities.title: What do you expect?
activities.instruction: You turn the linked isolator off. What happens to the three phase feeds at the outlet?
activities.explanation: The linked contacts operate together. Trace the protective earth separately. It goes straight to the outlet.

options.label: Only the phase nearest the handle is disconnected
All three are disconnected

activities.title: Connect 400 V three-phase / 230 V phase-neutral · L1 to Linked three-pole illustrative breaker · L1IN
activities.instruction: With the simulated supply off, connect 400 V three-phase / 230 V phase-neutral · L1 to Linked three-pole illustrative breaker · L1IN. Use the core marked L1.
activities.explanation: First phase of a three-phase supply. → Incoming L1 terminal of its separately modelled linked contact path. Pair it with L1OUT. Matching phase/neutral identities matter; mechanical linkage does not join the poles electrically.

activities.title: Connect 400 V three-phase / 230 V phase-neutral · L2 to Linked three-pole illustrative breaker · L2IN

activities.title: Connect Industrial socket linked isolation · L1OUT to Five-contact industrial outlet · L1
activities.instruction: With the simulated supply off, connect Industrial socket linked isolation · L1OUT to Five-contact industrial outlet · L1. Use the core marked L1.

activities.title: Connect 400 V three-phase / 230 V phase-neutral · PE to Five-contact industrial outlet · PE
activities.instruction: With the simulated supply off, connect 400 V three-phase / 230 V phase-neutral · PE to Five-contact industrial outlet · PE. Use the core marked PE.
activities.explanation: Supply earth. The earth connection runs alongside the meter. → Earth connection for the fitting. The earth path stays connected when the switch opens.

activities.title: Enable the simulated supply
activities.instruction: After completing the connections, leave resistance mode, then turn on the supply.
activities.explanation: Use voltage mode to check a powered circuit. Switch off all sources before testing continuity.

activities.title: Complete five-contact outlet
activities.instruction: Watch what the circuit does now.
activities.explanation: All active phases are available.

activities.title: Open linked socket isolation
activities.instruction: Open Industrial socket linked isolation.
activities.explanation: Linked isolation removes outlet operating state.

expectedObservations.title: Linked isolation removes outlet operating state

activities.title: Measure across the load
activities.instruction: Place red on Five-contact industrial outlet · L1 and black on Five-contact industrial outlet · N. Record the voltage with the controls in this position.
activities.explanation: Compare each outlet phase to neutral and the phase pairs to one another. One good pair cannot tell you that every phase is present. If you see zero, check the switch position.

activities.title: Read the current in one wire
activities.instruction: Select the conductor from 400 V three-phase / 230 V phase-neutral · L1 to Linked three-pole illustrative breaker · L1IN and record the current in amps.
activities.explanation: The meter shows the current in this wire. Where the circuit splits, the branches can carry different currents.

activities.title: Check the wire for a break
activities.instruction: Turn off all sources, then measure resistance between Industrial socket linked isolation · L3OUT and Five-contact industrial outlet · L3. Take the meter out of resistance mode before switching the power back on.
activities.explanation: A low resistance shows a path between the probes. If two wires reach the same point, the meter can still find a path around a break.

activities.title: What explains what you saw?
activities.instruction: Why are the isolator contacts linked?
activities.explanation: The linked contacts operate together. Trace the protective earth separately. It goes straight to the outlet.

options.label: So one handle opens the switched conductors together
So moving the handle changes the order of the phases

activities.title: Repair the fault
activities.instruction: Use your readings to find what went wrong. Repair it, then reset any device that tripped.
activities.explanation: Run a fresh test to check the repair.

activities.title: Retest the operating sequence
activities.instruction: Choose Test circuit to check your repair.
activities.explanation: The bench tries the lesson controls again using your wiring.

challenge.title: Diagnose: Five-contact industrial socket and isolation
challenge.briefing: The socket has two phases but the third phase is missing.
challenge.hint: Follow the missing phase from the isolator output to the same marking at the socket.
challenge.answer: The wire between isolator L3OUT and socket L3 is open. The two remaining phases cannot confirm a complete three-phase supply.

activities.title: Connect Stop · normally closed · NC to Motor overload and NC control contact · 95

activities.explanation: Normally closed path from COM: opens when the button is held pressed and closes on release. It can interrupt a maintained request if wired in that request path. → Normally closed contacts 95–96. An overload trip opens them. When they are wired in series with the coil, the contactor drops out and the motor stops.

challenge.title: Diagnose: Three-phase DOL motor starter
challenge.briefing: The motor starts, then stops as soon as you lift your finger.
challenge.hint: Follow the starter’s auxiliary output 14 back to coil A1.
challenge.answer: The wire from 14 to A1 is open. Start supplies the coil while held, but the auxiliary contact cannot maintain that supply afterwards.

activities.title: Enable the simulated supply
activities.instruction: After completing the connections, leave resistance mode, then turn on the supply.
activities.explanation: Use voltage mode to check a powered circuit. Switch off all sources before testing continuity.

activities.title: Direction starter begins stopped
activities.instruction: Watch what the circuit does now.
activities.explanation: motor operating load power stops.

activities.title: Start forward
activities.instruction: Press and release Start · momentary normally open. Watch what stays on.
activities.explanation: Forward phase sequence is observed. forward contacts close. reverse contacts open.

activities.title: Forward operation
activities.instruction: Watch what the circuit does now.
activities.explanation: Forward phase sequence is observed. forward contacts close. reverse contacts open.

activities.title: Stop before reversal
activities.instruction: Press and release Stop · normally closed. Watch what stays on.

activities.title: Select reverse
activities.instruction: Move Forward / reverse request to its second position.

activities.title: Start reverse
activities.instruction: Press and release Start · momentary normally open. Watch what stays on.
activities.explanation: Reverse phase sequence is observed. forward contacts open. reverse contacts close. Reverse has the actual mechanical pairing. Forward has reciprocal mechanical pairing.

expectedObservations.title: Reverse has the actual mechanical pairing

activities.title: Reverse operation
activities.instruction: Watch what the circuit does now.
activities.explanation: Reverse phase sequence is observed. forward contacts open. reverse contacts close. Reverse has the actual mechanical pairing. Forward has reciprocal mechanical pairing.

expectedObservations.title: Reverse has the actual mechanical pairing

activities.title: Measure across the load
activities.instruction: Place red on Reversible externally star-linked motor · U1 and black on Reversible externally star-linked motor · U2. Record the voltage with the controls in this position.
activities.explanation: Check each coil separately. While one direction is in, the other coil must remain out. Motor direction here follows the supplied phase order. If you see zero, check the switch position.

activities.title: Read the current in one wire
activities.instruction: Select the conductor from 400 V three-phase / 230 V phase-neutral · L1 to Linked three-pole illustrative breaker · L1IN and record the current in amps.
activities.explanation: The meter shows the current in this wire. Where the circuit splits, the branches can carry different currents.

activities.title: Check the wire for a break
activities.instruction: Turn off all sources, then measure resistance between Forward / reverse request · A and Reverse contactor · mechanical pair · 21. Take the meter out of resistance mode before switching the power back on.
activities.explanation: A low resistance shows a path between the probes. If two wires reach the same point, the meter can still find a path around a break.

activities.title: What explains what you saw?
activities.instruction: What is different about the reverse contactor’s wiring?
activities.explanation: Swapping any two phases reverses the phase order. The two contactors are interlocked so they cannot apply both connections at once.

options.label: Two phases change places
One phase is left disconnected

activities.title: Repair the fault
activities.instruction: Use your readings to find what went wrong. Repair it, then reset any device that tripped.
activities.explanation: Run a fresh test to check the repair.

activities.title: Retest the operating sequence
activities.instruction: Choose Test circuit to check your repair.
activities.explanation: The bench tries the lesson controls again using your wiring.

challenge.title: Diagnose: Interlocked forward/reverse motor starter
challenge.briefing: Forward is selected and Start operates the run circuit, but the forward contactor stays out.
challenge.hint: Trace the forward selector output into the reverse contactor’s normally closed auxiliary contact.
challenge.answer: The wire from selector A to reverse terminal 21 is open. The reverse contactor can be released and still have no forward command to pass through its interlock.

challenge.title: Diagnose: Six-terminal star-delta motor starter
challenge.briefing: Star works during starting. At changeover it releases, but delta never pulls in.

activities.title: Enable the simulated supply
activities.instruction: After completing the connections, leave resistance mode, then turn on the supply.
activities.explanation: Use voltage mode to check a powered circuit. Switch off all sources before testing continuity.

activities.title: Remove second heater-stage request
activities.instruction: Open Stage B temperature demand.
activities.explanation: stage-a contacts close. stage-b contacts open.

activities.title: Open common heater safety limit
activities.instruction: Open Independent high-temperature safety limit.
activities.explanation: stage-a contacts open. stage-b contacts open.

activities.title: Measure across the load
activities.instruction: Place red on Stage 1 phase 1 element · L and black on Stage 1 phase 1 element · N. Record the voltage with the controls in this position.
activities.explanation: Compare total power with one stage and with both. Check the stage coils to distinguish a single thermostat opening from the common high limit opening. If you see zero, check the switch position.

activities.title: Read the current in one wire
activities.instruction: Select the conductor from 400 V three-phase / 230 V phase-neutral · L1 to Linked three-pole illustrative breaker · L1IN and record the current in amps.
activities.explanation: The meter shows the current in this wire. Where the circuit splits, the branches can carry different currents.

activities.title: Check the wire for a break
activities.instruction: Turn off all sources, then measure resistance between Stage B temperature demand · OUT and Heater stage B · A1. Take the meter out of resistance mode before switching the power back on.
activities.explanation: A low resistance shows a path between the probes. If two wires reach the same point, the meter can still find a path around a break.

activities.title: What explains what you saw?
activities.instruction: What is different about the common high-temperature cut-out?
activities.explanation: Each stage has its own control. Both share the high-temperature cut-out, so either stage can be stopped on overtemperature.

options.label: It stops only the most recently selected stage
It can stop both stages

activities.title: Repair the fault
activities.instruction: Use your readings to find what went wrong. Repair it, then reset any device that tripped.
activities.explanation: Run a fresh test to check the repair.

activities.title: Retest the operating sequence
activities.instruction: Choose Test circuit to check your repair.
activities.explanation: The bench tries the lesson controls again using your wiring.

challenge.title: Diagnose: Staged three-phase heater bank
challenge.briefing: Both stages call for heat, but only the first bank heats.
challenge.hint: Read the stage B thermostat output and the voltage at the second contactor coil.
challenge.answer: The wire from thermostat B to stage B coil A1 is open. The common limit still supplies stage A, so that bank continues to heat.

Yes

activities.title: Connect Linked three-pole illustrative breaker · L1OUT to Stop · normally closed · COM
activities.instruction: With the simulated supply off, connect Linked three-pole illustrative breaker · L1OUT to Stop · normally closed · COM. Use the core marked control.
activities.explanation: Outgoing L1 terminal of its separately modelled linked contact path. Pair it with L1IN. Matching phase/neutral identities matter; mechanical linkage does not join the poles electrically. → Common connection of the separate changeover contact. This is a supplied contact circuit, not the coil or a neutral reference.

activities.title: Connect Remote stop · NC · NC to Motor overload and NC control contact · 95
activities.instruction: With the simulated supply off, connect Remote stop · NC · NC to Motor overload and NC control contact · 95. Use the core marked control.
activities.explanation: Normally closed path from COM: opens when the button is held pressed and closes on release. It can interrupt a maintained request if wired in that request path. → Normally closed contacts 95–96. An overload trip opens them. When they are wired in series with the coil, the contactor drops out and the motor stops.

activities.title: Connect Motor overload and NC control contact · 96 to Start · momentary normally open · COM

activities.title: Connect Motor overload and NC control contact · 96 to Two-station motor contactor · 13

activities.explanation: Normally closed contacts 95–96. An overload trip opens them. When they are wired in series with the coil, the contactor drops out and the motor stops. → Normally open auxiliary contacts. When the contactor pulls in, 13 joins 14. activities.title: Measure across the load
activities.instruction: Place red on Three-phase motor · externally linked star · U1 and black on Three-phase motor · externally linked star · U2. Record the voltage with the controls in this position.
activities.explanation: Read coil voltage after each release. Compare what happens at Stop with what happens when you merely let go of Start. If you see zero, check the switch position.

activities.title: Read the current in one wire
activities.instruction: Select the conductor from 400 V three-phase / 230 V phase-neutral · L1 to Linked three-pole illustrative breaker · L1IN and record the current in amps.
activities.explanation: The meter shows the current in this wire. Where the circuit splits, the branches can carry different currents.

activities.title: Check the wire for a break
activities.instruction: Turn off all sources, then measure resistance between Remote stop · NC · NC and Motor overload and NC control contact · 95. Take the meter out of resistance mode before switching the power back on.
activities.explanation: A low resistance shows a path between the probes. If two wires reach the same point, the meter can still find a path around a break.

activities.title: What explains what you saw?
activities.instruction: Why does either Stop button work?
activities.explanation: Either Start button can energise the same coil. Opening either Stop contact breaks the path that keeps the coil on.

options.label: Both Stop contacts are in the same holding circuit
Each Stop button disconnects one motor winding

activities.title: Repair the fault
activities.instruction: Use your readings to find what went wrong. Repair it, then reset any device that tripped.
activities.explanation: Run a fresh test to check the repair.

activities.title: Retest the operating sequence
activities.instruction: Choose Test circuit to check your repair.
activities.explanation: The bench tries the lesson controls again using your wiring.

challenge.title: Diagnose: Motor control from two stations
challenge.briefing: Both Stop buttons are released, but neither Start button can pull in the starter.
challenge.hint: Trace the common feed out of the remote Stop contact and into overload terminal 95.
challenge.answer: The wire from station B’s NC Stop output to overload 95 is open. Neither Start button nor the holding contact has a complete coil feed.

activities.title: Enable the simulated supply
activities.instruction: After completing the connections, leave resistance mode, then turn on the supply.
activities.explanation: Use voltage mode to check a powered circuit. Switch off all sources before testing continuity.

activities.title: Try upstream before downstream
activities.instruction: Press and release Start · momentary normally open. Watch what stays on.
activities.explanation: upstream contacts open.

activities.title: Invalid start sequence remains inhibited
activities.instruction: Watch what the circuit does now.
activities.explanation: upstream contacts open.

activities.title: Start downstream
activities.instruction: Press and release Start · momentary normally open. Watch what stays on.

activities.title: Start permitted upstream
activities.instruction: Press and release Start · momentary normally open. Watch what stays on.
activities.explanation: downstream contacts close. upstream contacts close.

activities.title: Valid running sequence
activities.instruction: Watch what the circuit does now.
activities.explanation: downstream contacts close. upstream contacts close.

activities.title: Stop downstream
activities.instruction: Press and release Stop · normally closed. Watch what stays on.
activities.explanation: downstream contacts open. upstream contacts open.

activities.title: Downstream stop removes upstream permission
activities.instruction: Watch what the circuit does now.
activities.explanation: downstream contacts open. upstream contacts open.

activities.title: Measure across the load
activities.instruction: Place red on Three-phase motor · externally linked star · U1 and black on Three-phase motor · externally linked star · U2. Record the voltage with the controls in this position.
activities.explanation: Compare the receiving starter’s feedback output with the control feed at the second starter. Check the coils as well as the motor states. If you see zero, check the switch position.

activities.title: Read the current in one wire
activities.instruction: Select the conductor from 400 V three-phase / 230 V phase-neutral · L1 to Linked three-pole illustrative breaker · L1IN and record the current in amps.
activities.explanation: The meter shows the current in this wire. Where the circuit splits, the branches can carry different currents.

activities.title: Check the wire for a break
activities.instruction: Turn off all sources, then measure resistance between Downstream conveyor starter · 14 and Stop · normally closed · COM. Take the meter out of resistance mode before switching the power back on.
activities.explanation: A low resistance shows a path between the probes. If two wires reach the same point, the meter can still find a path around a break.

activities.title: What explains what you saw?
activities.instruction: Why does stopping the receiving conveyor also stop the feed belt?
activities.explanation: The feed belt needs a closed contact from the receiving belt’s starter. When the receiving belt stops, that contact opens.

options.label: Both motors are connected to the same starter output
Its starter contact opens the feed belt’s control path

activities.title: Repair the fault
activities.instruction: Use your readings to find what went wrong. Repair it, then reset any device that tripped.
activities.explanation: Run a fresh test to check the repair.

activities.title: Retest the operating sequence
activities.instruction: Choose Test circuit to check your repair.
activities.explanation: The bench tries the lesson controls again using your wiring.

challenge.title: Diagnose: Sequential two-motor conveyor control
challenge.briefing: The receiving belt runs. The feed belt still refuses to start.
challenge.hint: Follow auxiliary terminal 14 on the receiving starter towards the upstream station’s Stop contact.
challenge.answer: The wire from the receiving starter’s 14 to the feed conveyor’s Stop COM is open. The first motor runs, but its run signal cannot reach the second starter.

activities.title: Enable the simulated supply
activities.instruction: After completing the connections, leave resistance mode, then turn on the supply.
activities.explanation: Use voltage mode to check a powered circuit. Switch off all sources before testing continuity.

activities.title: Default duty A
activities.instruction: Watch what the circuit does now.
activities.explanation: Duty A operates. Duty B stays stopped.

activities.title: Transfer duty to B
activities.instruction: Move Duty selection A / B to its second position.
activities.explanation: Duty A releases. Duty B operates without backfeed.

activities.title: High-level assist
activities.instruction: Turn on the call from High-level assist.
activities.explanation: Separate assist contact requests A. Separate assist contact requests B.

activities.title: Measure across the load
activities.instruction: Place red on Three-phase motor · externally linked star · U1 and black on Three-phase motor · externally linked star · U2. Record the voltage with the controls in this position.
activities.explanation: Read the two coil voltages for normal demand and again at high level. Assist can hide a fault in an individual duty path. If you see zero, check the switch position.

activities.title: Read the current in one wire
activities.instruction: Select the conductor from 400 V three-phase / 230 V phase-neutral · L1 to Linked three-pole illustrative breaker · L1IN and record the current in amps.
activities.explanation: The meter shows the current in this wire. Where the circuit splits, the branches can carry different currents.

activities.title: Check the wire for a break
activities.instruction: Turn off all sources, then measure resistance between Duty selection A / B · A and A duty OR assist · 1. Take the meter out of resistance mode before switching the power back on.
activities.explanation: A low resistance shows a path between the probes. If two wires reach the same point, the meter can still find a path around a break.

activities.title: What explains what you saw?
activities.instruction: What does the duty selector choose at normal water level?
activities.explanation: The duty selector picks the first pump. A separate float calls the second pump when one is no longer enough.

options.label: Which pump runs first
Whether both pumps run together

activities.title: Repair the fault
activities.instruction: Use your readings to find what went wrong. Repair it, then reset any device that tripped.
activities.explanation: Run a fresh test to check the repair.

activities.title: Retest the operating sequence
activities.instruction: Choose Test circuit to check your repair.
activities.explanation: The bench tries the lesson controls again using your wiring.

challenge.title: Diagnose: Duty/standby pumps and high-level assist
challenge.briefing: Normal level calls for pump A, but A stays off. B can run when selected. Leave high-level assist off while checking.
challenge.hint: Trace the A output of the duty selector to the first pump’s request junction.
challenge.answer: The wire from duty A to its request junction is open. B still has its own route. The assist path can still supply A and conceal that missing duty feed.

activities.title: Inspect 400 V three-phase / 230 V phase-neutral
activities.instruction: Open 400 V three-phase / 230 V phase-neutral and choose Show terminals. Find where its wires go.

activities.explanation: Linked three-phase overcurrent interruption. A trip on one monitored pole opens the linked device.

activities.title: Inspect PLC-commanded starter

activities.explanation: A coil operates linked power contacts and separate auxiliary contacts.

activities.title: Inspect Motor overload and NC control contact
activities.instruction: Open Motor overload and NC control contact and choose Show terminals. Find where its wires go.
activities.explanation: Motor current trips an auxiliary control contact. It only stops the motor if the control circuit uses that contact correctly.

activities.title: Inspect Isolated 24 V control supply

activities.explanation: An isolated DC control supply with a documented voltage and power limit.

activities.title: Inspect PLC input/output interface abstraction
activities.instruction: Open PLC input/output interface abstraction and choose Show terminals. Find where its wires go.
activities.explanation: A powered logic block maps wired permissive inputs to real output contacts.

activities.title: Inspect Workpiece-present sensor
activities.instruction: Open Workpiece-present sensor and choose Show terminals. Find where its wires go.
activities.explanation: A powered sensor supplies a switched live output when its condition is met.

activities.title: Inspect Machine-ready permission
activities.instruction: Open Machine-ready permission and choose Show terminals. Find where its wires go.
activities.explanation: A powered sensor supplies a switched live output when its condition is met.

activities.title: Inspect Controller secondary status

activities.explanation: A low-power indicator shows the actual voltage across its terminals.

activities.title: What do you expect?
activities.instruction: Only one of the two required inputs is on. What happens to the starter command?
activities.explanation: The PLC checks the two inputs before switching its starter output. Its separate status output can stay on even when the motor stops.

options.label: It switches off
It stays on as long as either input is on

activities.explanation: Check the control supply, both input voltages, output COM and the coil circuit. Power at the PLC electronics alone cannot show that Q1 has a supply to switch. If you see zero, check the switch position.

activities.title: Read the current in one wire
activities.instruction: Select the conductor from 400 V three-phase / 230 V phase-neutral · L1 to Linked three-pole illustrative breaker · L1IN and record the current in amps.
activities.explanation: The meter shows the current in this wire. Where the circuit splits, the branches can carry different currents.

activities.title: Check the wire for a break
activities.instruction: Turn off all sources, then measure resistance between Workpiece-present sensor · OUT and PLC input/output interface abstraction · I1. Take the meter out of resistance mode before switching the power back on.
activities.explanation: A low resistance shows a path between the probes. If two wires reach the same point, the meter can still find a path around a break.

activities.title: What explains what you saw?
activities.instruction: What does AND mean in this PLC programme?
activities.explanation: The PLC checks the two inputs before switching its starter output. Its separate status output can stay on even when the motor stops.

options.label: Either input can turn the output on by itself
Both required inputs must be on at the same time

activities.title: Repair the fault
activities.instruction: Use your readings to find what went wrong. Repair it, then reset any device that tripped.
activities.explanation: Run a fresh test to check the repair.

activities.title: Retest the operating sequence
activities.instruction: Choose Test circuit to check your repair.
activities.explanation: The bench tries the lesson controls again using your wiring.

challenge.title: Diagnose: PLC permissives and motor output interface
challenge.briefing: The PLC is on and the two field conditions are present, but the motor never gets a run command.
challenge.hint: Compare the signal leaving the presence sensor with I1 at the controller.
challenge.answer: The wire from the presence sensor output to PLC I1 is open. The two-input AND condition never becomes true, so the starter remains off.

challenge.title: Diagnose: Conceptual safety relay and monitored machine starter

activities.title: Enable the simulated supply

activities.title: Close cupboard door
activities.instruction: Close the cupboard.
activities.explanation: strip operating load power stops.

activities.title: Open cupboard door
activities.instruction: Open the cupboard.
activities.explanation: strip receives operating load power.

activities.title: Measure across the load
activities.instruction: Place red on Cupboard strip · + and black on Cupboard strip · −. Record the voltage with the controls in this position.
activities.explanation: Put one probe on each strip terminal. Expect about 24 V with the door open and near zero with it closed. If you see zero, check the switch position.

activities.title: Read the current in one wire
activities.instruction: Select the conductor from 240 V study supply · Ireland nominal 230 V · L to Illustrative RCBO · 16 A / 30 mA · LIN and record the current in amps.
activities.explanation: The meter shows the current in this wire. Where the circuit splits, the branches can carry different currents.

activities.title: Check the wire for a break
activities.instruction: Turn off all sources, then measure resistance between Cupboard door contact · closed with door open · L1 and Cupboard strip · +. Take the meter out of resistance mode before switching the power back on.
activities.explanation: A low resistance shows a path between the probes. If two wires reach the same point, the meter can still find a path around a break.

activities.title: What explains what you saw?
activities.instruction: The door is shut. Why is there still 24 V at the driver?
activities.explanation: A magnet on the door moves a switch contact. In this cupboard the contact closes when the magnet moves away.

options.label: The door switches the driver’s mains supply
The door switches the strip feed

activities.title: Repair the fault
activities.instruction: Use your readings to find what went wrong. Repair it, then reset any device that tripped.
activities.explanation: Run a fresh test to check the repair.

activities.title: Retest the operating sequence
activities.instruction: Choose Test circuit to check your repair.
activities.explanation: The bench tries the lesson controls again using your wiring.

challenge.title: Diagnose: Light a cupboard when its door opens
challenge.briefing: Opening the cupboard leaves the strip dark.
challenge.hint: Check the door contact output with the cupboard open, then check the positive pad on the strip.
challenge.answer: The wire from the door contact to the strip’s positive terminal is open. Moving the door works the contact, but its output never reaches the strip.

activities.title: What explains what you saw?

challenge.title: Diagnose: Dim a strip with pulses

activities.title: Enable the simulated supply
activities.instruction: After completing the connections, leave resistance mode, then turn on the supply.
activities.explanation: Use voltage mode to check a powered circuit. Switch off all sources before testing continuity.

activities.title: Bring metal to the sensor
activities.instruction: Bring metal near the sensor.
activities.explanation: pilot receives operating load power.

activities.title: Move the target away
activities.instruction: Move the metal away.
activities.explanation: pilot operating load power stops. Sensor supply stays present.

activities.title: Measure across the load
activities.instruction: Place red on Target indicator · + and black on Target indicator · −. Record the voltage with the controls in this position.
activities.explanation: Measure from the output to negative with the indicator connected. With the target close, the output should approach 24 V. If you see zero, check the switch position.

activities.title: Read the current in one wire
activities.instruction: Select the conductor from 240 V study supply · Ireland nominal 230 V · L to Illustrative RCBO · 16 A / 30 mA · LIN and record the current in amps.
activities.explanation: The meter shows the current in this wire. Where the circuit splits, the branches can carry different currents.

activities.title: Check the wire for a break
activities.instruction: Turn off all sources, then measure resistance between Inductive proximity sensor · PNP · OUT and Target indicator · +. Take the meter out of resistance mode before switching the power back on.
activities.explanation: A low resistance shows a path between the probes. If two wires reach the same point, the meter can still find a path around a break.

activities.title: What explains what you saw?
activities.instruction: Which wire should change voltage as the target comes and goes?
activities.explanation: Two wires keep the sensor powered. The third wire changes state when it detects the metal.

options.label: The switched output wire
The permanent positive supply wire

activities.title: Repair the fault
activities.instruction: Use your readings to find what went wrong. Repair it, then reset any device that tripped.
activities.explanation: Run a fresh test to check the repair.

activities.title: Retest the operating sequence
activities.instruction: Choose Test circuit to check your repair.

challenge.title: Diagnose: Sense a metal target with three wires
challenge.briefing: The sensor is powered but the indicator does not follow the target.
challenge.hint: With the target close, compare the sensor output with the positive terminal on the indicator.
challenge.answer: The switched output wire from the sensor to the indicator is open. Brown and blue still power the sensor, but the third wire cannot supply the load.

challenge.briefing: The bell rings and the relay operates but the courtesy light remains dark.
challenge.hint: Hold the entrance push. If the bell and relay operate, follow the DC side from the relay contact to the courtesy lamp.
challenge.answer: The wire from the relay’s NO contact to the courtesy lamp is open. The AC bell and coil still have their own complete circuit.
